the native membrane-bound FMO-reaction-center supercomplexes in green sulfur bacteria are composed of two reaction centers and 4 FMO trimers, which are arranged in a specific manner, and that the chlorosomes in green sulfur bacteria contain the RC-FMO complexes.

we have identified the native architecture of a supercomplex comprising two reaction centers and a single FMO trimer in Chlorobaculum and that the photosynthetic units in Chlorobaculums are composed of chlorosome and a pool of RC-FOM supercomplexes.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the structural analysis of the FMO protein and the native FMO-reaction-center complexes from the green sulfur bacterium Chlorobaculum (Chlorobium) tepidum, which is the first report on the structural analysis of a supercomplex from this bacterium.
the structure of the native FMO-reaction centers in C. tepidum, which is the most detailed study of the native supercomplexes in green sulfur bacteria.
a detailed analysis of the photosynthesizing supercomplexes of green sulfur bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FMO protein is a native component of the photosynthesizing membrane of green sulfur bacteria.

the photosynthetic apparatus of C. tepidum is composed of the reaction center and the FMO protein that is organized into the RC-FMO super-complexes, which are attached to the membrane by the CsmA protein.
the native photosynthetic unit in Chlorobaculum contains 12 RCs and 24 FMOs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to observe and analyze the native FMO-reaction centers supercomplexes in C. tepidum membranes.
we have shown the native architecture of photosynthetic superstructures in green sulfur bacteria and that we have provided a structural framework for understanding their functioning in vivo.
the structure of the supercomplexes of the photosynthesizing machinery of Chlorobaculum is now well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FMO protein, which is usually considered a peripheral protein of the photosynthesizing membrane, is in fact a part of the native photosynthetic superstructure.
the FMO protein is not just a light-harvestant, but also an important structural component of the photosynthesizing unit.
the native architecture of FMO is different from the structure determined by crystallography.
